liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Fire on the Mountain** (1 review, 1 other source): Attendee says everyone went wild during Fire; crowd was a rowdy Friday-night one; Lightning flashes during the first chorus, prompting more audience cheers [4][10]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Scarlet a raging version and says the second set is excellent throughout [9]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Odd crowd cheering occurs because the skylit roof let lightning flash right above the band during the song [16]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Reviewer finds Franklin's has its moments but is filled with repetitious vamps, typical of the era [17]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Reviewer, usually not a fan of Rooster, likes this one [18]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 other source): Bobby sings Get Up, Stand Up lyrics during this song [4]
- Band opens with a clean, energetic Half-Step; Jerry is in good voice throughout [17]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd81-05-15 s1t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd81-05-15 s1t02 Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd81-05-15 s1t03 Franklin's Tower**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd81-05-15 s1t04 New Minglewood Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd81-05-15 s1t05 Dire Wolf**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd81-05-15 s1t06 Cassidy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd81-05-15 s1t07 Candyman**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd81-05-15 s1t08 Little Red Rooster**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-05-15.142954.senn421.wise.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 171 min [1]
- **gd81-05-15.senn.munder.9008.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 162 min; rated 4.05/5 by 19 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is pleasant; Jerry's guitar licks seem pushed up in the mix, and the rowdy crowd is audible; Reviewer praises the audience tape for capturing the old gym's acoustics and the crowd going wild with the band responding; Reviewer, who also taped the show, finds this recording better than their own, though with somewhat too much audience noise [9][11][16]
- **gd1981-05-15.sbd.miller.86783.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 175 min; rated 3.64/5 by 14 [5]
- **gd1981-05-15.142953.senn421.wise.miller.clugston.flac1648**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 171 min [2]

## Around the show

- Storm raged at the end of the first set; skylight lightning flashes draw crowd cheers during Looks Like Rain, around 7:45 [10]
- Attendee drove from Long Island and got tickets while stuck in a traffic jam; arena roof has a skylight [10]
- Reviewer was a Rutgers junior on the music committee that put on the show; ticket line of over 600 people waited overnight [14]
- A thunder and lightning storm accompanied the show [14]
- Show was at the RAC on Livingston College campus in Piscataway, across the Raritan River from New Brunswick [20]
- Reviewer considers 1981 one of the best post-1974 years, though short of the band's early-seventies heights [16]
- Of the 5-15-81 and 5-16-81 pair, reviewer finds this night the better one, with stronger performance and setlist [17]
- Reviewer thinks the next night's show is better than this one [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-05-15.142954.senn421.wise.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: flac24/96 Jim Wise's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII-C90)(located at the soundboard)Transfer Info:Master Cassettes… [1]. Also: Jim Wise recorded the show on an audience master; this is a fresh transcription, pitch corrected; An AKG CE-1 source supplies a short patch in Don't Ease Me In and a 4:23 patch in Drums [1]
- **gd81-05-15.senn.munder.9008.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Sennheiser 421 [3]. Also: Sennheiser 421 from front of board, to cassette master, DAT, then CD; came via Charlie Miller and was seeded by Willy [3]
- **gd1981-05-15.sbd.miller.86783.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Cassette -> Reel -> Dat (48k) [5]. Also: Soundboard-labeled mix built from a Sennheiser 421 audience source, patched with an AKG CE-1 source for short sections [5]
- **gd1981-05-15.142953.senn421.wise.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: flac16/48 Jim Wise's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII-C90)(located at the soundboard)Transfer Info:Master Cassettes… [2]

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1981-05-15 Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1981-05-15-backstage-pass/) [24]
